name: Timor-Leste

findings.local_actor: Cabos de Timor-Leste, E.P. (state-owned cable operator); Government of Timor-Leste
findings.builder: Alcatel Submarine Networks (cable); DXN Limited, Australia (cable landing station)
findings.financier: Government of Timor-Leste; Australian Infrastructure Financing Facility for the Pacific (AUD 7.2m, partial)
findings.summary: The 607 km Timor-Leste South Submarine Cable, supplied by ASN and landed at Bebonuk, Dili in June 2024, links Dili to Australia via Vocus's North-West Cable System and entered commercial operation under state-owned Cabos de Timor-Leste in July 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor rule: ASN (French, state-owned since 2024) supplied the cable, so pole third; operator is domestic and onward link is Australian (Vocus). ASN named by DCD and Converge Digest; government speech and Telecom Review confirm launch but not the builder. USD 1.4m DXN contract covers the landing station only, so no cable value recorded. still_current true from the July 2026 launch.

findings.summary: Telkomcel launched 4G in Timor-Leste on Ericsson equipment, including Ericsson Radio System LTE RAN, a virtual Evolved Packet Core and NFV infrastructure, as a modernisation of its existing network.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson (Sweden) supplies RAN and core, so pole third. Tier 5 for a launched commercial 4G service; site count not stated. Pre-2020 and not reconfirmed as current. Single opened source (S1 vendor release), so medium per spec.

findings.controller: Not stated (Zchwantech, Malaysia, as technology partner)
findings.summary: Malaysian firm Zchwantech announced a planned strategic partnership with Timor-Leste, starting with a feasibility study for a Tier 3+ National Sovereign AI Cloud and Data Centre, followed by AI-enabled digital ID and border systems.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: future owner-operator of the sovereign AI cloud not stated; 'sovereign' and planned technology transfer suggest domestic, Zchwantech involvement suggests third. Tier 1: stated intent, no instrument type named and feasibility study not yet reported as started. No S1/S2 source; both opened reports likely derive from a company release. No model or chip vendor named.
